summary: Defines a protocol for carrying ISDN Q.921 user messages over IP using SCTP, between a signaling gateway and a media gateway controller. The gateway receives ISDN signaling on a standard ISDN interface and passes it on. It replaces RFC 3057 and is on the standards track.

eli5.summary: Old phone lines have their own way of setting up calls. This memo lets those call-setup messages ride across the internet inside a different envelope, so equipment in different places can still work together.

questions: what is an application server process
subtitle: How a signaling gateway hands ISDN call-control messages to a remote controller over SCTP.

tldr.problem: ISDN signaling arrives at a gateway on a standard ISDN interface, but the call processing that understands it may live in a different machine reachable only over IP. The Q.921 layer is terminated at the gateway, so the layer above it needs a way to talk across the network.
tldr.mechanism: IUA is a thin adaptation layer that carries the Q.921/Q.931 boundary primitives, plus management and failover messages, between a Signaling Gateway and a Media Gateway Controller. It runs over SCTP and uses Interface Identifiers to tell D channels apart.
tldr.outcome: IUA gives redundant call-processing servers a defined way to come up, take traffic, fail over and be monitored. RFC 4233 obsoletes RFC 3057 and has been updated by RFC 5133.

today: RFC 4233 is a Proposed Standard published in January 2006. It obsoletes RFC 3057 and has been updated by RFC 5133.

sections.title: What IUA Is For
sections.content:
The ISDN Q.921-User Adaptation Layer (IUA) defines a protocol for backhauling ISDN Q.921 user messages over IP using the Stream Control Transmission Protocol (SCTP). Here, a Q.921-User is any upper layer that uses the services of Q.921, such as Q.931 or QSIG. A Signaling Gateway (SG) receives ISDN signaling over a standard ISDN interface and terminates Q.921, then passes the layer above it to a Media Gateway Controller (MGC) where the peer Q.931 layer lives.

The delivery mechanism SHOULD support three things: transport of the Q.921/Q.931 boundary primitives, communication between Layer Management modules on the SG and MGC, and management of the active SCTP associations between them. The document covers ISDN Primary Rate Access and Basic Rate Access, point-to-point and point-to-multipoint operation, Facility Associated Signaling, Non-Facility Associated Signaling and NFAS with a backup D channel. QSIG needs no different procedures.
sections.eli5: Imagine the front desk of a hotel takes your phone call but the person who decides what to do lives in another city. IUA is the private line that carries the front desk's messages to that person.

sections.title: Gateways, Application Servers and Redundancy
sections.content:
IUA is the adaptation module in a larger signaling transport architecture. It is recommended to run over SCTP, which brings packet-oriented delivery, sequenced delivery within multiple streams, multi-homing for network-level fault tolerance, resistance to flooding and masquerade attacks, and segmentation to path MTU. Where redundancy is handled below the transport layer, TCP MAY be used instead.

Incoming Q.921-User messages at the SG are assigned to an Application Server (AS) by their Interface Identifier. An AS is in practice an ordered list of Application Server Processes (ASPs), such as primary and backup MGC instances. IUA supports an n+k redundancy model, where n ASPs are the minimum needed and k are available to take over. 1+1 active/standby and simplex 1+0 are subsets of it.

By default the SG acts as server and the ASP as client, so ASPs SHOULD initiate the SCTP association. The registered port for IUA over both SCTP and TCP is 9900. It is recommended to use a separate SCTP stream for each D channel, and management messages SHOULD use stream 0.
sections.eli5: A busy call center has one main agent and a few backups waiting. The gateway sends each call to whoever is on duty and quickly switches to a backup if the main agent disappears.

sections.title: The IUA Message Format
sections.content:
Every IUA message starts with a common header of Version, Reserved, Message Class, Message Type and a 32-bit Message Length that counts the header and any parameter padding. All fields use network byte order. The only defined version is 1 (Release 1.0). The Reserved byte SHOULD be zero and is ignored by the receiver.

Parameters follow in type-length-value form: a 16-bit tag, a 16-bit length and a value, padded with zero bytes so each parameter is a multiple of 4 bytes. The padding is not counted in the parameter length, a sender SHOULD NEVER pad with more than 3 bytes, and mandatory parameters come before optional ones.

Data-carrying messages add an IUA message header holding an Interface Identifier (integer, tag 0x1 and always length 8, or text, tag 0x3) and a DLCI parameter (tag 0x5, length 8). The DLCI holds the Q.921 SAPI (6 bits) and TEI (7 bits) and is coded as in Q.921. Integer Interface Identifiers MUST be supported, text ones MAY be.
sections.eli5: Every message has a label on the front saying what kind of message it is and how long it is, followed by labeled boxes of details. Each box is padded so they all line up neatly.

sections.title: Carrying Q.921 Primitives
sections.content:
The Q.921/Q.931 Boundary Primitives Transport (QPTM) class has message types 1 to 10: Data Request and Indication, Unit Data Request and Indication, Establish Request, Confirm and Indication, and Release Request, Confirm and Indication. Each corresponds to a DL-ESTABLISH, DL-RELEASE, DL-DATA or DL-UNIT DATA primitive at the Q.921 boundary.

The MGC controls the state of the D channel. When it wants the D channel in service it sends an Establish Request, and the SG passes the matching Q.921 primitive to its Q.921 entity and maps the response back to an Establish Confirm or a Release message. A Release carries a Reason: RELEASE_MGMT (0x0), RELEASE_PHYS (0x1), RELEASE_DM (0x2) or RELEASE_OTHER (0x3). Only MGMT, DM and OTHER are valid in a Release Request.

Data messages carry the upper layer message, such as Q.931 or QSIG, in a Protocol Data parameter (tag 0xe). Data uses the acknowledged information transfer service and Unit Data the unacknowledged one.
sections.eli5: When the controller wants a phone line switched on or off, it sends a short request and the gateway reports back. The actual call messages are tucked inside parcels that the gateway just passes along.

sections.title: ASP and AS States
sections.content:
The SG tracks the state of every ASP in every AS. An ASP is ASP-DOWN (unavailable or its SCTP association is down; the initial state), ASP-INACTIVE (the peer is available but application traffic is stopped) or ASP-ACTIVE (the peer is available and traffic is active). Events that change ASP state include peer messages, SCTP indications such as Communication Down and Restart, and local management.

The AS itself is AS-DOWN (all ASPs down), AS-INACTIVE (some ASP inactive, none active), AS-ACTIVE (at least one ASP active) or AS-PENDING. AS-PENDING begins when the last active ASP goes inactive or down. The SG starts a recovery timer T(r) and queues incoming messages. If an ASP becomes active before T(r) expires, the queued messages go to it. Otherwise the SG discards them and the AS moves to AS-INACTIVE if some ASP is inactive, or to AS-DOWN if not.
sections.eli5: Each backup agent is either off duty, at their desk but not taking calls, or on a call. If the last agent on a call walks away, the switchboard holds callers for a few seconds hoping someone picks up.

sections.title: Bringing an ASP Up and Active
sections.content:
After the SCTP association is up, the ASP sends ASP Up, optionally with an ASP Identifier. The SG marks the ASP inactive and MUST answer with ASP Up Ack, even if the ASP was already inactive. The ASP waits for the ack before sending anything else. It then sends ASP Active with a mandatory Traffic Mode Type, Over-ride (0x1) or Load-share (0x2), and optionally the Interface Identifiers it wants, as integers, ranges or text. The SG replies with ASP Active Ack and starts sending traffic. The ASP MUST wait for that ack before sending Data, or it risks message loss.

In Over-ride mode the newly active ASP takes all traffic for the AS from any currently active ASP. In Load-share mode it shares traffic with the others. Only one mode may be used within an AS. ASP Down and ASP Inactive reverse these steps, and each has an acknowledgement. An ASP that sends one of these messages starts timer T(ack), whose default is 2 seconds, and may retransmit until it gets the ack.

The SG sends Notify messages as autonomous indications, for example AS-INACTIVE, AS-ACTIVE or AS-PENDING, and for cases such as an alternate ASP becoming active. Heartbeat and Heartbeat Ack messages are optional and recommended when IUA runs over a transport other than SCTP, which has its own heartbeat.
sections.eli5: A backup agent first says 'I am here', waits for a reply, then says 'put calls through to me', and waits for a second reply before picking up the phone.

sections.title: Errors and TEI Status
sections.content:
An Error message carries an Error Code and optional Diagnostic Information that SHOULD include the offending message. Codes include Invalid Version (0x01), Invalid Interface Identifier (0x02), Unsupported Message Class (0x03), Unsupported Message Type (0x04), Unsupported Traffic Handling Mode (0x05), Unexpected Message (0x06), Protocol Error (0x07), Unsupported Interface Identifier Type (0x08), Invalid Stream Identifier (0x09) and further TEI, SAPI and ASP Identifier errors up to 0x0f. Error messages MUST NOT be generated in response to other Error messages.

In ordinary ISDN switches the Layer Management for Q.921 and Q.931 sit together. When Q.931 is backhauled they do not, so the TEI Status Request, Confirm and Indication messages let the two sides share whether a TEI is ASSIGNED (0x0) or UNASSIGNED (0x1). A TEI Query message, added in this version, asks the SG to answer with TEI Status Indications.
sections.eli5: If a message is wrong or arrives at the wrong time, the receiver sends back a note with a number saying what was wrong. It never replies to a note with another note, so the two sides cannot get into an endless argument.

sections.title: Security, IANA and Timers
sections.content:
For security, the considerations in RFC 3788, "Security Considerations for SIGTRAN Protocols", apply. IANA assigned IUA the SCTP Payload Protocol Identifier value 1. New message classes, message types and parameters can be added through an IETF Consensus action, and a receiver that gets an unsupported message type MUST answer with an Error of Unsupported Message Type.

The RFC suggests default timer values: T(r) 3 to 5 seconds, T(ack) 2 to 5 seconds and a heartbeat timer T(beat) of 30 seconds. Compared with RFC 3057, this version adds the TEI Query message, explains the DLCI format, and aligns the ASP and AS procedures and message formats with the companion SIGTRAN adaptation specifications RFC 3331 and RFC 3332.
sections.eli5: The memo points to a shared safety guide for this family of protocols, gets an official number from the registry, and suggests how long to wait before trying again.
